newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears Samsung takeover of AST.
newsitem.headline: EU clears Samsung takeover of AST.

text.p: The European Commission on Tuesday cleared Samsung Electronics's offer to buy all the shares in U.S. computer maker AST that it does not already own, but said it may fine the South Korean firm for being late in filing for EU approval.
A Commission source said later that the fine would be a minimum 100,000 European currency units ($113,500) and that it was sure to happen.
The Commission, the EU's competition watchdog, said Samsung gained control of AST in January 1996.

Samsung Electronics Co Ltd announced in April a tender offer for all remaining shares in the California-based maker of personal computers. But at the time it already owned a stake of about 46 percent.
Samsung's offer to buy all AST shares is still running. It expires on June 17.

Under EU merger control law, the acquisition by a company of a controlling stake in another firm or any other corporate concentrations with a European dimension must be submitted to the Commission for clearance no more than one week after being concluded or publicly announced.
The final fine will depend on Samsung's reasons for failing to seek regulatory approval wherever required and on the opinion of a committee of competition experts from the EU's 15 states.

In clearing the deal, the Commission said that AST Research Inc's and Samsung's sales in the European Union were small -- below 5.0 percent -- and virtually no overlap would result from the operation.
